title: Warmly Sliced German Pork Pastrami
description: A savory German dish featuring thinly sliced pork pastrami, crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, paired with a creamy sesame butter.

ingredients.name: Curing mixture (salt, sugar, pink curing salt, black pepper, coriander seeds)

instructions: Combine the curing mixture, water, white vinegar, sesame oil, sesame seeds, brown sugar, black pepper, and coriander seeds in a bowl and mix well.
Rub the curing mixture all over the pork shoulder, making sure to coat it evenly.
Place the pork shoulder in a large ziplock bag or a non-reactive container, and refrigerate for at least 2 days or up to 4 days.
After the curing time, remove the pork shoulder from the bag or container and rinse it under cold running water to remove any excess cure.
Pat the pork shoulder dry with paper towels and set it aside.
Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add a small amount of oil to the pan and sear the pork shoulder until browned on all sides, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Transfer the pork shoulder to a cutting board and let it rest for 5 minutes before slicing it thinly against the grain.
In a small bowl, mix the mantecare emulsifier with a small amount of water until it forms a smooth paste.
Add the sour cream to the bowl and mix until well combined.
Season the sesame butter with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve the thinly sliced pork pastrami on a crusty bread roll or on a bed of sauerkraut, topped with the sesame butter and chopped fresh dill.
